title: Ministry Of Social Justice And Empowerment To Organise Departmental Summit ‘Samaveshi Niti Sankalp’ On November 18–19, 2026, In The National Capital
subtitle:
Focus on Strengthening Centre-State Collaboration Towards Viksit Bharat@2047
Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi To Grace The Valedictory Session
Two-Day Summit to Feature Four Thematic Sessions, Six Comprehensive Deliberations and Digital Exhibition Showcasing Key Initiatives of the Ministry
More Than 13,500 Responses Received from Over 450 Districts to Inform Policy Deliberations and Strengthen Ground-Level Implementation
States and Union Territories to Share Best Practices, Address Implementation Challenges and Develop Time-Bound Action Plans for Inclusive Development
body_text: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment will organise the Departmental Summit ‘Samaveshi Niti Sankalp’ on November 18–19 (Wednesday & Thursday) at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan in the National Capital, as a significant step towards realising the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. The Summit is the third in the series of Departmental Summits envisioned by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, to foster collective ownership of national priorities and accelerate development outcomes through closer collaboration between the Centre and the States. Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, is scheduled to grace the Valedictory Session. The two-day Summit aims to provide an institutional platform for meaningful dialogue, shared responsibility and coordinated action between the Union and State Governments on key policy priorities, programmes, initiatives and strategies for strengthening social justice and inclusive development. Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice, Shri Sudhansh Pant said in preparation for the Summit, the Ministry has undertaken systematic consultations with field-level functionaries and stakeholders to ensure that ground-level experiences and implementation-related insights form policy deliberations. He said a series of video conferences were held with State and Union Territory officials, while feedback was invited on four thematic areas from stakeholders within and outside the Government. The consultation exercise received an overwhelming response, with more than 13,500 responses from over 450 districts, whileas these valuable inputs have been incorporated into the background notes prepared for the Summit, the Secretary said. Shri Pant said the Departmental Summit model brings together political leadership and senior officials from the Union and State Governments to deliberate on important issues relating to the Ministry's mandate. It provides an opportunity to share successful practices, address implementation challenges, explore innovative approaches and develop time-bound action plans to ensure effective implementation of government initiatives and delivery of their benefits to intended beneficiaries, he said. The Secretary said the Summit will focus on four key thematic areas, namely, ‘Reimagining Prevention and Drug Demand Reduction Strategy for a Nasha Mukt Bharat’, ‘One Nation, One Scholarship Portal – Accessible Scholarships, Empowered Students’ , ‘Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden’ and ‘Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat’ . These themes reflect the Ministry's commitment to strengthening social inclusion, enhancing access to welfare initiatives and promoting the empowerment of all sections of society, he added. Giving the details, Shri Pant said the deliberations will be conducted through four breakout sessions and two full-house sessions, enabling comprehensive discussions on the identified themes. All States and Union Territories will be provided dedicated opportunities to make presentations during the breakout sessions and share their views during the full-house sessions, Shri Pant said. He added two experts will also share insights on international best practices to enrich the discussions and facilitate the adoption of innovative approaches for effective programme implementation. As part of the Summit, delegates will visit a Digital Exhibition showcasing key initiatives and technological interventions of the Ministry, that will  feature integrated portals such as ‘Samavesh’ and ‘e-Anudan’ , mobile applications developed for field-level operations and success stories highlighting the impact of various schemes and programmes of the Ministry, the Secretary said. Shri Pant noted the digital exhibition will provide an opportunity to showcase technology-driven interventions and innovative approaches supporting effective implementation and improved delivery of services to beneficiaries. It will also highlight the Ministry's efforts towards strengthening institutional mechanisms and promoting inclusive development through digital platforms and field-level initiatives, he added. The Secretary said the Summit is expected to facilitate meaningful exchange of ideas, promote mutual learning among States and Union Territories, and strengthen collaborative strategies for building an inclusive, equitable and empowered society. Shri Pant informed that the key outcomes and action plans, along with defined timelines for their implementation, will be presented before the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, during the valedictory session. The Secretary noted the guidance of the Hon’ble Prime Minister will stimulate the collective resolve of the Centre and the States, providing  renewed impetus to the collective efforts and setting the course for decisive, coordinated and time-bound action towards achieving the agreed outcomes  and advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.
